newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian corporate profits rise 5.7 pct in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Canadian corporate profits rise 5.7 pct in Q4.

text.p: Canadian corporations posted their second consecutive quarterly increase in operating profits in the fourth quarter, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
It said operating profits rose 5.7 percent to a record high of C$25.7 billion following a 7.4 percent jump in the third quarter.
Two-thirds of the industry groups registered stronger gains in the quarter but the bulk of the gain was concentrated in the financial sector, which saw an 18.9 percent surge in profits.
Wood and paper and motor vehicles and accessories offset gains in the energy sector, resulting in little overall change in the non-financial industries.

The return on equity for all corporations rose to 8.8 percent in the fourth quarter -- its strongest in seven years -- from 7.5 percent and 6.7 percent in the third and second quarters. After-tax profits jumped 19.2 percent in the fourth quarter, while total equity increased marginally.

Annual profits for 1996 rose to a record C$95.3 billion from C$93.8 billion in 1995, the fourth consecutive annual increase. Much of the recovery in the past three years originated in export-based industries.

Chartered banks' operating profits rose to C$11.9 billion in 1996 from C$7.8 billion in 1995. Petroleum and natural gas industry profits rose 31.6 percent to C$13.6 billion in 1996. Wood and paper operating profits fell in the year to C$4.6 billion from C$10.8 billion.
